source.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning in a Handful of Trials using Probabilistic Dynamics Models
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 31

confidence_rationale: Canonical, highly-cited NeurIPS paper establishing that a learned forward/dynamics model should emit input-conditional predictive uncertainty (aleatoric, per-input) and that propagating that uncertainty into action selection materially improves behaviour. High mapping fidelity to SD-063's architecture (E2 forward model emits per-prediction spread -> E3 gates commitment), lowered because PETS represents aleatoric uncertainty with a Gaussian-NLL head + ensemble rather than the distribution-free quantile form SD-063 prefers, and it uses uncertainty for trajectory-sampling planning rather than a single commit/hold gate.
failure_signatures: PETS separates aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty by ensembling; a single-head E2 quantile spread conflates them, so the SD-063 head cannot be assumed to isolate the environment-noise component the way PETS's trajectory sampling does.

PETS obtains its per-input aleatoric variance from a Gaussian-NLL probabilistic network -- exactly the head form that lost to quantile_pinball in V3-EXQ-712 -- so the paper supports 'conditional uncertainty feeds action' without endorsing SD-063's specific distribution-free form.

mapping.source_claim_statement: An uncertainty-aware probabilistic dynamics model that captures input-dependent aleatoric (and, via ensembling, epistemic) uncertainty, with that uncertainty propagated through trajectory sampling during planning, closes the asymptotic performance gap between model-based and model-free RL while using 8-125x fewer samples.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-063's core architectural bet -- that the E2 world-forward model should carry a per-input predictive-uncertainty signal that downstream action machinery (E3 commitment gating) conditions on -- is the same design pattern PETS validates at scale: a forward model whose uncertainty output is conditional on the current (state, action) query and is consumed by the action-selection stage, rather than a single global noise scalar.
mapping.mapping_caveat: PETS uses uncertainty for sampling-based trajectory optimisation (MPC/CEM), not a binary commit/hold gate, and represents aleatoric uncertainty with a Gaussian-NLL head plus an ensemble for epistemic uncertainty. SD-063 proposes a single distribution-free quantile head and a commit-gating consumer; the paper supports the general principle (conditional forward-model uncertainty improves action decisions) but not the specific head form or the specific consumer, and says nothing about the SD-031 agency-residual concern.
mapping.source_context: Continuous-control benchmarks (cartpole, half-cheetah, reacher, pusher) in simulation; deep neural dynamics models trained from a handful of trials.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (foundational NeurIPS result, widely replicated). Mapping fidelity strong on the architectural principle but not on the specific quantile head or commit-gate consumer. Transfer risk moderate: control-RL substrate differs from REE's E1/E2/E3 latent stack, and PETS's aleatoric/epistemic separation via ensembling is not what SD-063 builds.
